newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand shares close firmer despite Dow's fall.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand shares close firmer despite Dow's fall.

text.p: * New Zealand shares close firmer on solid volumes
* Mutual fund money reallocation seen beneficial for NZ shrs
* NZ equities seen representing good value at current levels
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
131 nil * NZSE-40 cap index
308 +2 * NZSC cap index -0.13 at 4,973.62
345 -2 * Volume NZ$75 million. Futures +3 at 1,115
656 +5 * Other movers - +13 +10
New Zealand shares closed firmer on Thursday on solid volumes despite weaker offshore markets.

"We've had a very good day on the New Zealand market," said Tim Koller at Merrill Lynch. "It closed up nearly eight points when all indications were that we would probably follow offshore markets and be down today."
The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 7.66 points stronger at 2,225.91 on turnover worth a healthy NZ$75 million.
Brokers said New Zealand equities were benefiting from a reallocation of mutual fund money around the world at the beginning of the new quarter.
"Our market has underperformed foreign markets this year, so relatively it's cheaper and people see value in our stocks at these levels," said Koller.
"A lot of our stocks haven't done anything for ages and really do appear to be fairly good buying."
Fletcher Challenge Energy was one of the star performers on the day, rising 13 cents to NZ$3.98.

During the session, FCL Energy said it had begun "sidetrack" operations in an attempt to increase recovery and production from its McKee oil field in Taranaki, on the west coast of New Zealand's North Island. Sidetracking is branching off an existing drill hole.
FCL Energy also announced changes to its hedge position.
Brokers noted there had been solid demand in Telecom, up five to $6.56, and Carter Holt Harvey, up one at $3.07. Brierley ended flat at $1.31 on high turnover of eight million shares.
